title: The Shepherd Who Stays
bigIdea: God does not just lead us to green pastures; he stays with us in the dark valleys too.

details: David speaks from experience: he was a shepherd himself
A shepherd's whole job is the good of the sheep
Green pastures and still waters are his idea, not ours
Rest is something we receive, not something we earn

outline.point: He walks with us through the valley
details: The psalm moves from talking about God to talking to God: "you are with me"
The valley is real, but it is something we walk through
Goodness and mercy pursue us all our days
The story ends at home with him

applications: Name one valley you are walking through and tell God about it this week.
Take ten quiet minutes each day without your phone.
Check in on someone in your small group who is having a hard week.
questions: What picture of God does Psalm 23 give us, and which line stood out to you?
Where in your life right now does it feel like a dark valley?
What is one way you can rest in God's care this week?
prayer: Lord, thank you for being my shepherd. Help me trust that you are with me, even in the valley.
